title: Adaptive min softening experiment notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note on the "adaptive min softening" experiment we ran across regional GPU fleets in May 2024. Goal: reduce scale oscillation and wasted pre-provisioned capacity while keeping p95 latency SLOs intact. This doc collects raw observations, heuristics that emerged, and a candidate runbook + config patch for further validation.

Background / motivation:
- Problem: we observe repeated scale-ups followed by immediate scale-downs (oscillation) in low-to-medium sustained traffic lanes (intermittent bursts from queued jobs, rampy traffic, and ML warmups). Hard min settings in some regions cause overprovisioning; very low mins cause frequent coldstarts and latency spikes.
- Existing mitigations tried: longer cooldown, larger scale steps, hysteresis windows. All helped but did not eliminate oscillation when bursts hit multiple regions with differing baseline utilization.

Key idea (adaptive min softening):
- Instead of a single static min per region, compute a soft_min that can be temporarily lowered when forecasted demand is low and there is confidence in cross-region fallback. Soft_min is bounded by a safe_hard_min (never below); soft_min reverts to configured min once rolling baseline utilization exceeds threshold.
- Complement with an "available-effective-gpu" signal that discounts GPUs reserved for long-running dedicated tenants and noisy-neighbor buffers. This prevents the autoscaler from double-counting capacity.

Experiment setup (May 8–20, 2024):
- Regions: us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1.
- Baseline fleet sizes pre-experiment: us-east-1: 120 GPUs (min 80, max 240), eu-west-1: 48 GPUs (min 24, max 96), ap-northeast-1: 36 GPUs (min 12, max 72).
- Soft_min window parameters tested (in each region):
  * soft_floor_factor: 0.6 (allow adjusting min down to 60% of configured min)
  * prediction_confidence_threshold: 0.75 (only reduce min when the short-term predictor confidence >= 0.75)
  * protection_hard_min: 0.4 (never go below 40% of configured min)
  * reversion_interval: 15m (soft_min lasts at most 15 minutes before re-eval)
- Signals used by autoscaler: queue_length_avg_1m, p95_inference_latency_1m, rolling_gpu_util_5m, pending_request_backlog, model_start_rate_1m.
- Control group: regions keeping static min/max/cooldowns.

Observations (high level):
- us-east-1: oscillation events reduced by ~42% (count of up-then-down cycles per 6h window) compared to baseline. p95 latency remained within SLO for 98.6% of requests (vs 98.1% baseline). Cost metric (short-term reserved GPU-hours) reduced ~7% during low-traffic nights.
- eu-west-1: saw less benefit; prediction_confidence often below 0.75 due to more spiky traffic from a few enterprise customers. When soft_min triggered incorrectly, there were transient p95 spikes (~200ms at peak) but there was no sustained outage.
- ap-northeast-1: capacity savings ~12% but a small increase in coldstart events for some models that rely on warm KV cache; those models had cache-hit degradation for ~1–3 minutes after reversion.

Root causes identified for residual oscillation and failures:
1) Predictor overfitting to seasonal patterns; when an unmodeled short burst occurred, soft_min lowered capacity prematurely and the autoscaler then ramped quickly back up, creating a smaller oscillation.
2) Cross-region routing assumptions not encoded in the autoscaler; fallback routing increased request arrival in a healthy region triggering cascades.
3) Mixed tenant reservations: reserved instances with soft affinity to a region were treated as available leading to underestimation of effective capacity.

Heuristics and emergent rules from the run:
- Only enable soft_min for "lane" groups with at least N=3 independent request origins (reduces single-customer vanity effects).
- Require two independent signals to agree before reducing min: predictor_confidence >= threshold AND rolling_gpu_util < util_floor for 10m.
- If p95 latency increases by >10% after a soft_min reduction, immediately revert and raise a temporary suppression window (30m) for soft_min in that region.
- When soft_min reduces capacity, pre-announce to routing layer (short TTL) so traffic can be rebalanced proactively if needed.

Candidate config patch (prototype JSON snippets live in linked PR):
- soft_min_enabled: true
- soft_min_factor: 0.6
- soft_min_hard_floor: 0.4
- soft_min_max_duration: 900  # seconds (15m)
- soft_min_agreement_required: 2  # number of signals
- predictor_model: rolling-AR-3 (experiment model id: ar3-v2)

Failure modes and rollback criteria:
- Rollback immediately if region exhibits sustained p95 > SLO for 30+ minutes OR if error rate increases by >0.5% absolute over baseline.
- Reversion if coldstart count for critical-model-set increases > 20% week-over-week during experiment window.

Operational runbook (quick):
1) Monitor 1-min dashboard (sheet link in artifacts) for soft_min_active_count and soft_min_revert_events.
2) If unexpected oscillation increases, flip feature flag: autoscaler.soft_min_enabled = false for offending region.
3) Post-mortem: run the evaluation script (linked) to extract traces and attach to INFRA-2345.

Action items and owners:
- Short term (this week): tighten predictor retraining cadence to daily for lane groups (owner: Ben Carter).
- Mid term: add reservation-aware capacity signal in autoscaler (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Long term: integrate routing-aware capacity planning (owner: Liam O'Connor + Networking).

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Evaluate softer reversion behavior (gradual ramp-up back to configured min instead of instant revert).
- Test combined soft_min + step-smoothing (small step sizes but longer cooldown) to see if we maintain SLO with more graceful capacity curves.
- Model-level warm caches: can we persist cache state across temporary downsized replicas to reduce coldstart pain?

Notes to self / rough logs (raw):
- 2024-05-09 03:12: saw 3 up/down cycles in us-east tied to a 7m spike at merchant-A endpoint; predictor confidence dropped to 0.22 then recovered.
- 2024-05-12 19:45: eu-west triggered soft_min while enterprise-X had scheduled batch job; manual revert performed. Add enterprise tag exclusion.

Concluding recommendation (for Q3 pilot):
- Run soft_min in "observe" mode for all regions for 2 weeks (no actual capacity reduction, only signal logging) to collect better ROC curves.
- If ROC looks good, enable soft_min behind feature flag with strict protections (hard_min floor, dual-signal agreement, routing announcement).
- Pair rollout with integration to billing/reservations signal so effective-available-gpu is accurate.

Appendix: useful links and dd logs
- Capacity sim sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aB2cFleetCapacitySim/edit#gid=0
- Jira: INFRA-2345 (experiment tracking), INFRA-2390 (reservation-signal), INFRA-2412 (warm-cache persistence)
- PR w/ prototype autoscaler code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/412

End of notes.
summary: Working notes describing the adaptive min softening experiment across regional GPU fleets; includes setup, observations, heuristics, runbook and next steps.
